case_name: Mahant Dooj Das (Dead) Through Lr v Udasin Panchayati Bara Akhara and Another
respondent:
Udasin Panchayati Bara Akhara and Another
Supreme Court of India

1  May  2008
C.A. No. 5060 of 2007
The Judgment was delivered by: P. P. Naolekar, J.
1.  The facts necessary for adjudicating the question involved are that the plaintiff-appellant (for convenience hereinafter referred to as "the plaintiff") filed a suit claiming decree for possession over the properties/lands [21 Bighas, 8 Biswa Kachhi Bhumi (land) No. Khasra 27M and 28M and Bhumi (land) 1 Bigha, 3 Biswa, 10 Biswanshi Kacchi No. Khasra 27M and 28M and Bhumi (land) 19 Bigha, 3 Biswa, 15 Biswansi Khasra No. 4M and Bhumi (land) 30 Bigha Kacchi No. Khasra 4M total Bhumi (land) 71 Bighas, 15 Biswa, 5 Biswansi Kacchi situated at Bhupatwala Kalan, Pargana Jwalapur, Distt. Saharanpur and houses and 4 boundary walls pakka and well with wheels and brick-kiln, garden and tube-well with oil engine and tin shed etc. which have been situated on the above mentioned land presently Khasra No. 4/5 (4/2
facts: The plaintiff-appellant filed a suit claiming decree for possession over the properties/lands
Mahant Tahal Dass initiated the plaintiff-Dooj Das as his chela on 23.7.1937 at the Dera of Bhetiwala, Tehsil Muktasar, District Ferozpur in accordance with the custom
The suit was filed on the allegations that Mahant Tahal Dass was Udasin of Panth of Revered Shrichand.
Budh Dass was never initiated as chela by Mahant Tahal Dass and, therefore, he had no right, title and interest over the suit lands.
The trial court decreed the suit of the plaintiff holding that the plaintiff was initiated as the eldest chela of Mahant Tahal Dass according to the custom

As regards jurisdiction of the civil court to try the suit and the valuation put by the plaintiff, it was held, while trying them as preliminary issue on 13.10.1969, that the civil court had jurisdiction to try the suit.
The lessee in fact created a dera on the spot by erecting buildings, installing tube-wells etc.
All these matters in controversy can only be decided by a competent civil court and, therefore, lower court has rightly upheld the jurisdiction of the civil court to try the suit.
issues: Whether after enforcement of the U.P. Urban Areas Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1956, the land in suit, stood vested with the State of U.P. by operation of law free from all encumbrances and stood settled with the Appellants (Defendant No.1 and 2) exclusively?
Whether the suit was barred by S. 331 of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950?
Whether the State of U.P. and the Gaon Sabha/Gaon Panchayat, were the necessary parties? If so, was the suit liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties?
petitioner_arguments: The plaintiff was initiated as the eldest chela of Mahant Tahal Dass according to the custom and the plaintiff became the heir and successor in respect of the properties of Mahant Tahal Dass.
Budh Dass, the transferor who was the chela of Tahal Dass, succeeded to the properties situated at Bhupatwala, Hardwar after the death of his Guru Mahant Tahal Dass.
respondent_arguments: Defendants Nos. 1 and 2 did not derive any right or title in the suit properties by the sale deed.
Budh Dass was never initiated as chela by Mahant Tahal Dass and, therefore, he had no right, title and interest over the suit lands.
court_reasoning: The trial court decreed the suit of the plaintiff holding that the plaintiff was initiated as the eldest chela of Mahant Tahal Dass according to the custom

As regards jurisdiction of the civil court to try the suit and the valuation put by the plaintiff, it was held, while trying them as preliminary issue on 13.10.1969, that the civil court had jurisdiction to try the suit.
The first appellate court held that plaintiff was the eldest chela of Mahant Tahal Dass and was duly installed as successor of the Mahant and he succeeded to the properties of his Guru.
holding: The trial court decreed the suit of the plaintiff holding that the plaintiff was initiated as the eldest chela of Mahant Tahal Dass according to the custom
C.A. Nos. 117/1976 and 118/1976 were dismissed and judgment and decree of the trial court was confirmed.
